title: Executable triage notebooks and captureable debug profiles for first responders
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds executable triage notebooks that bundle live query snippets, log slices and a lightweight debug profile capture tool. No behavioral changes to production handlers; purely opt-in observability and responder utilities.
description: Motivation: Our on-call flow often requires reconstructing state from scattered logs, traces and ad-hoc scripts. This PR introduces a reproducible, executable triage notebook format and a small debug-profile capture utility so first responders can collect a self-contained diagnostic bundle to accelerate TTR and post-incident analysis. Design summary: 1) triage notebooks (Markdown + executable code cells) that can be rendered in plain HTML or executed with the bundled runner to replay queries against a specified time window; 2) a captureable debug profile binary (profilerc) that collects pprof-like CPU/heap/trace artifacts and a lightweight process snapshot designed to be safe in production (rate-limited, size-capped, redacts env secrets); 3) templates and a single-command builder to create a tarball containing notebook, logs, trace slices, and profiles suitable for attaching to incidents or uploading to internal storage. Changes include a new notebook kit (pkg/triage), runner (cmd/triage-runner), templates (internal/templates/triage_notebook.md), documentation (docs/oncall/triage-guide.md), and E2E tests that validate notebook build and bundle contents. Checklist: - [x] Design review with SRE and Incident Response (ENG-2024) - [x] Security review for secrets redaction and KMS usage - [x] Tests for bundling and size caps - [x] Docs and quickstart snippet - [x] Backwards compatible: tools are opt-in and activated by an env var How to use: run `triage-runner build --since 2026-03-01T09:00Z --until 2026-03-01T09:20Z --include-traces` to produce `triage-bundle-<ts>.tgz`. The bundle unpacks into a notebook.html, queries.sql, logs/*.log, and profiles/*.pprof. Commit summary: - 5c9a8d7 feat(triage): add notebook templates and builder - a2b7f11 feat(capture): add profilerc with redact and size limits - c43d9e2 feat(cli): triage-runner CLI and basic e2e harness - 99b1b5b test: add e2e tests for bundle validation - d5f2e44 docs: triage quickstart and runbook example Changed files (high level): cmd/triage-runner/main.go, pkg/triage/notebook.go, pkg/triage/builder.go, pkg/capture/profilerc.go, internal/templates/triage_notebook.md, docs/oncall/triage-guide.md, test/e2e/triage_bundle_test.go, Makefile updates, CI workflow `.github/workflows/triage.yml`. Tests & CI: initial pipeline failed on the first run due to a nondeterministic timestamp in the notebook header which broke snapshot tests; fixed by normalizing timestamps in test harness (see commit c43d9e2) and reran CI. Final CI: all checks green, coverage for new pkg/triage at 82%. Security review notes: the profilerc performs explicit redaction of environment variables using a denylist, and the collector is disabled by default in production builds. Performance: profilerc uses sampling and caps output size to avoid I/O amplification; no measurable change to handler latency when used with the default 1s sampling for 10s (verified in perf-canary). Migration notes: no runtime migration required; teams must opt in to publish or collect bundles. Merge: Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-03 by Maya Chen. Follow-ups: add richer DAG of notebook cells, integrate with incident-bot to auto-attach a starter notebook on incident create (ENG-2087).

merge_commit_message:
chore(triage): add executable triage notebooks and profilerc (ENG-2024)

Adds an opt-in diagnosics bundle builder and a small safe profiler for first responders. Includes templates and quickstart.
manual_testing_notes: Locally ran triage-runner against a synthetic log store and verified bundle contents. Performed a dry run of profilerc on a staging instance with TRIAGE_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true and verified redaction and size limits. E2E harness validates expected file types inside tarball and enforces size caps.
security_notes: Profilerc redacts env vars matching internal denylist, strips out Authorization headers from captured traces, and supports encryption of bundles via KMS key specified at build time. Review conducted by security team on 2026-02-18.
